reply.summary: Measure the bore, piston skirt, piston-to-cylinder clearance and ring clearances before reuse. Inspect for scoring or cracks first—acceptable dimensions don’t make damaged parts reusable.

**Check the bore and piston for scoring, cracks and damaged ring grooves before measuring.** Clean off carbon first; measure the parts cool, using a bore gauge and outside micrometer—not calipers.

For your **2022 YZ125’s stock cylinder and piston**, Yamaha gives:

| Check | How to measure | Yamaha’s figure |
|---|---|---|
| Cylinder bore | Measure front-to-back and side-to-side at three heights: six readings. Record all six. | Standard **54.000–54.014 mm**; wear limit **54.064 mm** |

turns.rider: What do I need to measure on the piston and cylinder before I reuse them?

reply.summary: Measure the bore in six places, the piston skirt, actual piston-to-cylinder clearance, both rings and the piston pin fit. Passing the bore wear limit alone does not make the piston and cylinder reusable.
reply.answer:
**The deciding measurement is actual bore minus actual piston diameter—not how clean they look.** These figures are Yamaha’s for the stock 2023 YZ250 piston and cylinder; an aftermarket piston needs its maker’s clearance instructions.

1. **Inspect first.** Clean off carbon without scratching anything. Look for vertical scoring, damaged plating, cracks, worn ring grooves and heat discoloration. Measurements do not override physical damage.
2. **Measure the cylinder with a dial bore gauge.** Measure front-to-back and side-to-side at three heights—six readings total. Record them all; use the **largest bore** for the clearance calculation. Differences reveal taper and out-of-round.
3. **Measure the piston with an outside micrometer**, across the skirt perpendicular to the pin, **17.5 mm (0.69 in) above the skirt bottom**. Calipers are not accurate enough for this decision.

| Check | Yamaha specification |
|---|---|
| Standard cylinder bore | **66.400–66.414 mm** |
| Cylinder bore wear limit | **66.464 mm maximum** |
| Standard piston skirt diameter | **66.352–66.367 mm**, depending on grade |
| Largest bore minus measured piston diameter | **0.045–0.050 mm** specified clearance |
| Top and second ring side clearance | **0.030–0.065 mm**; **0.100 mm maximum** |
| Top and second ring end gap | **0.95 mm maximum**, each |

Check side clearance with each ring in its cleaned groove. For end gap, square each ring near the bottom of the bore with the piston crown, then measure with feeler gauges. **The end-gap maximum is a wear limit, not a new-ring fitting target.**

Also check the pin and small-end bearing: pin diameter must not be below **17.975 mm**, piston pin bore must not exceed **18.040 mm**, and specified pin-to-bore clearance is **0.004–0.020 mm**. Reject a grooved or blue pin and a heat-discolored bearing.
